investigacion.base:
Based on what's available now, this would resolve **No**. No country other than the DRC is anywhere near 100 confirmed cases. Getting there by the end of 2026 would take a new, sustained chain of transmission somewhere outside the DRC, and none has been reported so far.

**Resolution source (WHO AFRO External Situation Reports)**
- The newest AFRO report my searches turned up is Weekly External Situation Report 13, Data as of 09 August 2026. It reported a cumulative total of 4,381 confirmed cases and 2,011 confirmed deaths as of 9 August 2026, covering the DRC and Uganda. There are probably later reports I didn't find, so check the AFRO page directly for the latest number and its per-country table.

**Latest counts**
- **WHO Disease Outbreak News, data as of 7 September:** a cumulative total of 6778 confirmed cases has been reported: 6757 in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (including two cases diagnosed in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and subsequently treated in Germany), 20 cases in Uganda and one case in France. WHO said new cases since 28 August were reported only in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
- **Wikipedia, as of about 26 September:** 8,088 confirmed cases in total, with Uganda still at 20. The two cases treated in Germany are counted under the DRC, and the US humanitarian worker who tested positive (reported 10 July) appears to be counted there too.
- **ECDC (about 28 September):** 78 new confirmed cases and 49 deaths since the previous report on 26 September, all in DRC provinces.

**Uganda, the only other country with local spread**
- On 28 July, the Ministry of Health of Uganda declared the end of the BVD outbreak in the country following 42 days without a new locally transmitted confirmed case being reported. Of these 20 cases, 15 were imported cases linked to travel from DRC.
- The count stalled early: it went from 19 cases as of June 17, 2026, to 20 by July 8, 2026.
- The Dutch public health institute (RIVM) noted on 2 September that WHO and Africa CDC had confirmed the end of the outbreak in Uganda.

**Risks that could still produce a Yes**
- The DRC epidemic is still growing. It's the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record, affecting 61 health zones in six provinces, including North and South Kivu, which border Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi.
- People are moving across borders. A case who died on 11 September in Sud-Ubangi had travelled from South Kivu, passing through Rwanda and Uganda before reentering and transiting DRC.
- There is no licensed vaccine or treatment specific to Bundibugyo, and insecurity limits detection.

**Base rates**
- Cases outside the DRC have mostly been single imports quickly contained (France, Germany) or small clusters (Uganda: 20 cases, with the last confirmed case in mid-June).
- Even during the 2018–20 North Kivu outbreak, with about 3,470 cases, Uganda had only 4 cases.
- Only the 2014–16 West Africa epidemic produced more than 100 cases in several countries.
- The biggest Bundibugyo outbreak before this one, Uganda in 2007, had 56 lab-confirmed cases.
- Getting from 0 to more than 100 confirmed cases in a new country within about 3 months would be historically unusual.

**Scheduled events**
- WHO AFRO keeps publishing weekly situation reports, and the last one released in 2026 decides the question.
- IHR Emergency Committee meetings continue (the second has already happened), and vaccine trials are rolling out.

**Prediction markets:** I didn't find any.

**Sources:**
- [1](https://www.afro.who.int/countries/democratic-republic-of-congo/publication/ebola-bundibugyo-virus-disease-outbreak-4)
- [2](https://www.who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news/item/2026-DON617)
- [3](https://www.ecdc.europa.eu/en/ebola-outbreak-democratic-republic-congo-and-uganda)
- [4](https://www.nicd.ac.za/bundibugyo-virus-disease-updates/)
- [5](https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/eid/article/32/10/26-1411_article)
- [6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Ebola_epidemic)

criterios: This question will resolve as Yes if any country other than the Democratic Republic of the Congo has >100 total confirmed cases of Bundibugyo ebolavirus during 2026.
letra_pequena:
The source for this question will be the last World Health Organisation [External Situation Report](https://www.afro.who.int/health-topics/ebola-disease) released during 2026. No other source will be used. 

This question will not re-resolve based on future revisions.
razonamientos:
**(a) Time left:** About 3 months. The question resolves on the last WHO AFRO External Situation Report released in 2026, around late December.

**(b) Status quo:** No. Uganda is the only non-DRC country with local transmission. It stalled at 20 confirmed cases and declared its outbreak over on 28 July. France has one case. The cases treated in Germany and the US case are counted under the DRC.

**(c) Reference class:** Cross-border spread from large DRC and Central African Ebola outbreaks.
- In 2018–20 there were about 3,470 cases, and Uganda had only 4.
- Only the West Africa epidemic of 2014–16 produced more than 100 cases in more than one country, and each of those countries took months of uncontrolled urban spread to get there.
- The largest earlier Bundibugyo outbreak, Uganda in 2007, reached 56 confirmed cases over several months.
- The base rate for a new country going from 0 to more than 100 confirmed cases within about 3 months is well under 5%. The current DRC epidemic is unusually large (8,000+ cases, still growing, bordering several countries), which raises the risk somewhat.

**(d) No scenario:** The DRC epidemic continues or slowly declines. Occasional imports into Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi or elsewhere are detected and contained, producing clusters well below 100. The final 2026 WHO AFRO report shows every non-DRC country far under the threshold.

**(e) Yes scenario:** An undetected chain seeded from North or South Kivu takes hold in an urban setting, such as Goma–Gisenyi into Rwanda, Bujumbura, or Kampala. Missing specific vaccines and treatments help it grow, and it exceeds 100 confirmed cases by December, as reported by WHO AFRO.

**(f) Technicalities:**
- Only the last WHO AFRO External Situation Report of 2026 counts.
- Cases must be confirmed, not probable, and attributed to a country other than the DRC. Imported cases counted under the DRC, like those treated in Germany, would not help.
- If the report tables are delayed or not released, a delay in reporting a real surge could also push the outcome toward No.

Probability: 4%

(a) **Time left:** About three months until the last WHO External Situation Report released in 2026, though that report could appear before December 31.

(b) **Status quo:** No. The reported count outside the DRC is far below the threshold; Uganda, the main concern, has 20 confirmed cases.

(c) **Reference class:** Large Ebola outbreaks in Central Africa have rarely produced more than 100 confirmed cases in a neighboring country. Even the 2018–20 DRC outbreak produced only four reported cases in Uganda. This is a small reference class, but it favors No.

(d) **No scenario:** Cross-border introductions remain isolated or cause small clusters, as they have so far.

(e) **Yes scenario:** An introduction into Uganda or another neighbor starts sustained transmission, adding at least 81 confirmed cases in Uganda before the decisive report.

(f) **Resolution technicality:** The threshold is **more than** 100 confirmed *Bundibugyo* cases in one country other than the DRC—not 100 exactly, and not cases merely treated abroad if the WHO report attributes them to the DRC. Only the last WHO External Situation Report released during 2026 counts.

Probability: 3%

(a) **Time left:** About three months, until the last WHO External Situation Report released in 2026.

(b) **Status quo:** No. The reported count outside the DRC is far below 101; Uganda, the only other country reported to have had local spread, has 20 confirmed cases.

(c) **Reference class:** Cross-border spread during major Ebola outbreaks is possible, but reaching more than 100 confirmed cases in another country is rare. The 2018–20 DRC outbreak produced only a handful of cases in Uganda; the 2014–16 West Africa epidemic is the notable counterexample.

(d) **No scenario:** The DRC outbreak continues, but exported cases are detected and contained before sustained transmission takes hold elsewhere.

(e) **Yes scenario:** An undetected chain of transmission grows rapidly in Uganda or another neighboring country, adding at least 81 confirmed cases in Uganda—or 101 in a country starting from zero—before year-end.

(f) **Resolution technicality:** The deciding evidence is **the last WHO External Situation Report released during 2026**, not later revisions or other sources. Cases must be confirmed *Bundibugyo ebolavirus* cases attributed to a country other than the DRC; the two patients treated in Germany, for example, are reportedly counted under the DRC.

The large and continuing DRC outbreak makes a new cross-border cluster plausible. But getting from the current counts to the threshold in the remaining time would require substantial sustained spread, so I give the status quo considerable weight.

Probability: 2%
